study type: Secondary analysis of a retrospective, observational cohort study
exposure: delivery hospital setting (academic or academic-affiliated vs community medical centers)
Known diagnosis of Marfan syndrome or Loeys-Dietz syndrome before delivery
cohort: Singleton pregnancies among patients with Marfan syndrome or Loeys-Dietz syndrome from 1990 to 2016
finding: Patients with Marfan syndrome or Loeys-Dietz syndrome delivering at academic hospitals had higher rates of operative vaginal delivery, while those delivering at community hospitals had higher rates of cesarean delivery for the indication of Marfan syndrome or Loeys-Dietz syndrome, despite lower frequencies of aortic root diameter >4.0 cm.
mod_finding: Operative vaginal delivery rates were higher at academic hospitals compared to community hospitals for women with a known diagnosis of Marfan syndrome or Loeys-Dietz syndrome before delivery (27.2% vs 15.1%, P=.03).
